title: Personal Trading Policy
body:
Personal Trading Policy
Owner: Compliance (maintained by Luis Bowen, KYC Specialist, on behalf of Marcus Bell, Chief Compliance Officer)
Last updated: 2026-08-13

Purpose
This policy sets out how Halcyon Ridge Capital employees may trade for their own accounts and for accounts of household members. It exists to prevent conflicts of interest, front-running, misuse of material non-public information (MNPI), and the appearance of any of these. It applies to every employee in the directory, including Trading, Wealth Management, Lending, M&A Advisory, Risk, Operations, Technology, Compliance and the Executive Office.

Who and what is covered
Covered persons are all employees, plus spouses or partners, dependent family members, and any account over which an employee has trading discretion or beneficial interest. Covered instruments include listed equities, ETFs, options, futures, fixed income, and digital assets. Exempt instruments are open-end mutual funds, US Treasuries, and broad-based index products on the approved exemption list kept by Compliance.

Disclosure of accounts
Within 30 days of joining, and annually thereafter, each employee must disclose all covered brokerage accounts to Compliance through the attestation form in HRIS. Changes, such as opening or closing an account, must be reported within 10 business days. Employees must arrange for duplicate statements and trade confirmations to be sent to Compliance.

Pre-clearance
All trades in covered instruments require pre-clearance from the Compliance team before the order is placed. Submit requests through the pre-clearance form; Compliance will check them against the restricted list and the watch list. Approval is valid for the trading day on which it is granted only. If you do not trade that day, you must request approval again. Compliance may deny a request without giving a reason.

Restricted and watch lists
The restricted list contains issuers where the firm holds MNPI or has an active role, including any issuer connected to a live M&A Advisory mandate. Members of Project Falcon and other wall-crossed teams are prohibited from trading in the relevant names and related securities for the duration of the engagement and until Compliance releases the name. The watch list is confidential and is used for surveillance, not for general distribution. Never discuss the contents of either list outside Compliance or the deal team.

Holding periods and prohibited activity
Positions must be held for at least 30 calendar days before being closed, except where Compliance grants a hardship exception. The following are prohibited at all times:
- Trading on MNPI or tipping others who may trade
- Front-running or trading ahead of client, desk, or firm orders
- Short-term speculative trading in names covered by your own team
- Participating in initial public offerings or private placements without written approval from the CCO
- Using firm systems, including OMS, PricingSvc, PositionStore, and ClientHub, to research or place personal trades

Special rules for Trading and Wealth Management
Traders and portfolio managers may not trade a security for themselves within 3 business days before or after a desk or client account trades it. Personal orders may not be entered in OMS or routed through firm execution channels. Wealth advisors and relationship managers must not use knowledge of pending client activity recorded in ClientHub or PortfolioMgr when making personal decisions.

Digital assets
Personal digital asset activity follows the same disclosure and pre-clearance rules. Please follow the #crypto-policy working group for updates on tokens that may be restricted because of client or counterparty activity.

Monitoring and surveillance
Compliance reviews disclosed statements against firm trading activity and the restricted list each quarter. Data from the firm's surveillance tooling and the DataLake is used to detect patterns. Employees must cooperate with any inquiry and provide records promptly.

Quarterly and annual attestations
Every quarter, employees must confirm that all personal trades were pre-cleared and that disclosed accounts are complete. An annual certification of compliance with this policy is required each January. Missing a deadline is escalated to your department head.

Breaches and escalation
Report suspected violations immediately to Compliance or to the CCO. Reports made in good faith are protected from retaliation. Violations may lead to trade reversal, disgorgement of profits, mandatory training, formal warning, suspension, or termination, and may be reported to regulators where required.

Questions
Post general questions in #compliance. For anything involving a specific trade or a possible conflict, contact Compliance directly rather than posting in a public channel. This policy is reviewed annually, or sooner if regulations or firm structure change.
